transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I'm here because I just can't seem to stay focused on anything. The main thing is I get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be trying to work on a job application, and then a car drives by outside, or my phone buzzes, or I just get some random idea in my head, and... I'm doing something completely different before I even notice I stopped what I was supposed to be doing. It's just really getting in the way of everything.
Have you struggled with this level of distraction for as long as you can remember, or is this a relatively new issue for you?

Yeah, it's been going on for as long as I can remember. Um, even back in elementary school, it was a problem. My teachers were always having to move my seat because I talked out of turn a lot. I also forgot my homework all the time, or I'd just rush through my worksheets and end up making a bunch of careless mistakes. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new issue for me.
Do you currently find it difficult to sit still for long periods, or do you often feel like you have to be constantly moving or doing something?

Yeah, definitely. It's really hard for me to just sit and relax. Even on days when I don't have anything going on, I'm always moving around. Like, I'll go from the kitchen, out to the garage, and then over to my game setup... it just feels like I'm supposed to be doing something all the time, even when there's nothing to do.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they are talking or acting on impulses before thinking about the consequences?

Yeah, I do that. I actually cut people off a lot. It happens especially with my mom, or, um, the counselor. It's just... an answer pops into my head, and I end up saying it before they're even done talking. I don't really mean to be rude, I just kind of blurt it out before thinking about it.
